subject: Service fallback & credit matrix — proposed compromise
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 18 Oct 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Draft SLA proposal for Stellar — uptime / credits / fallback

Ben / Laura — sending the first pass of language for the Stellar engagement. Stellar asked for an elevated uptime guarantee (their operations team mentioned "financial settlement windows" as a driver) and they pushed hard on a 99.99% target with minimal credits.

Attached: SLA_v2_redlines.pdf and a proposed monthly-credit-matrix.xlsx that maps uptime bands to service credits. High level of what I'm proposing in this draft: 
- Default hosted offering: 99.95% monthly uptime (this aligns with current public profile). Credits scale: small for 99.9-99.95, larger for 99.8-99.9, cap at 50% invoice for <99.5.
- Dedicated option (reserved capacity): optional 99.99% for customers willing to commit to a 12‑month reserved plan + a 15% uplift on monthly fees. If they opt in, we accept tighter credits but add stricter operational commitments: scheduled maintenance windows, regional failover configuration, and a higher support SLA.
- Latency carve-outs: include a clear maintenance & third-party dependency carveout and a 15-minute transient window for network flaps inside the same POD.
- Fallback policy: automatic fallback to a compatible model variant during capacity spikes; we won't treat these brief fallbacks as downtime unless KV/cold-start prevents request completion.

Key asks for this thread: 
1) Ben — legal points we should be prepared for (credit cap requests from procurement).
2) Laura — pricing owner: confirm 15% uplift is defensible for Dedicated 99.99 option given our unit economics.
3) Marcus — any ops constraints I missed (maintenance cadence, cross-region failover lead time).

If you agree with this approach I'll send the external proposal to ops@stellarpayments.com and loop in their legal. I tried to keep the hosted baseline conservative and make the 99.99 option conditioned on Dedicated + price.

Thanks — Diego

--
Diego Fernandez

From: Ops Team <ops@stellarpayments.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karen Cho <kcho@stellarpayments.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 10:07:00 -0500
Subject: Re: Draft SLA proposal for Stellar — uptime / credits / fallback

Diego — thanks for the draft. Overall this looks promising but legal and platform have pushed back on a few items: 

1) Uptime target: Stellar's platform requires a 99.99% monthly uptime for settlement windows during business hours (06:00–20:00 ET). For off‑hours they can accept 99.95, but their procurement team wants the 99.99 guarantee for the Hosted product unless we can show an equivalent escape (e.g., Dedicated requirement).

2) Credit cap: legal insists on a 25% maximum credit of monthly charges. Their procurement team will not sign anything with unlimited or >25% exposure.

3) Latency sensitivity: their engineering team flagged potential impact from fallbacks — if you fallback to a different model variant that increases tail latency above 300ms, that will affect their transaction batching. They want explicit language around what constitutes a "non-compliant" request when fallback is in effect.

Attached: Stellar_SLA_redlines.pdf (legal) — high level comments inline.

Can we propose: 99.99 for Dedicated only, but if Redwood can offer a 30-minute regional failover SLA and a 25% credit cap, Stellar can accept the Dedicated condition. If you cannot get the Dedicated-only condition, their procurement will walk.

-Kevin (on behalf of Stellar Ops)

--
Ops Team
Stellar Payments
ops@stellarpayments.com

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 19 Oct 2026 13:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft SLA proposal for Stellar — uptime / credits / fallback

Diego — quick internal rundown after reading Stellar's redlines. TL;DR: negotiable but need guardrails. My recommended approach: 

- Keep Hosted baseline at 99.95 with the credit matrix you drafted. Moves us off blanket exposure.
- Offer 99.99 ONLY on Dedicated with these conditions: 12‑month commit, 15% fee uplift (call it "High Availability Premium"), and a hard cap of 25% credits per month (matches Stellar legal ask).
- For latency-sensitive fallbacks: offer an SLA addendum that defines two classes: "degraded (fallback with completed request)" vs "failed (request not completed)". Only the latter counts toward uptime calculations. Explicitly allow transient model‐variant fallback not to trigger downtime unless request fails or latency exceeds a negotiated tail latency (suggest 300ms for critical paths).
- For regional failover: confirm Ops can support a 30-minute *recovery* objective for cross-region routing changes for Dedicated customers who opt into active‑passive config. Marcus — can you confirm plausibility and estimated SRE runbook scope?

If Marcus confirms, I think we can accept Stellar's 25% credit cap in the Dedicated case, but we should retain the Hosted 99.95 baseline. We should also ask for a 60‑day notice on any change to traffic patterns that materially increase peak qps (this helps capacity planning).

I suggest Diego send a concise customer-facing compromise email: offer Dedicated 99.99 with 25% cap + HA premium; keep Hosted 99.95. Keep legal tight on language around fallback/latency.

-Ben

--
Ben Carter
Director, Enterprise Sales
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.ai>
To: Ops Team <ops@stellarpayments.com>
Cc: Karen Cho <kcho@stellarpayments.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft SLA proposal for Stellar — uptime / credits / fallback

Kevin / Karen — thanks for the quick feedback and the redlines. We've discussed internally and can propose the following compromise (summary below; full language attached in SLA_v2_redlines.pdf):

1) Baseline (Hosted): 99.95% monthly uptime. Credits: tiered matrix as attached. Host customers keep standard fallback protections; transient model fallbacks that complete requests will be considered "service continuity" (i.e., not downtime) unless they cause request failure or sustained tail latency over 300ms for a majority of affected requests.

2) Elevated offering (Dedicated): 99.99% monthly uptime available as an opt-in addendum for customers purchasing Dedicated capacity with a 12‑month commitment + a 15% HA premium to monthly fees. For Dedicated 99.99 we will accept a 25% monthly credit cap (matches your legal ask).

3) Regional failover / recovery objective: for Dedicated HA customers we will provide an active-passive configuration with a 30‑minute recovery objective for cross-region re-routing. This is operationalized via runbooks and DR playbooks; we'll share the runbook excerpts during onboarding.

4) Maintenance & carveouts: scheduled maintenance (pre-notified) and third-party infra failures are excluded from uptime calculations per the redline language. We will commit to a maximum of two scheduled maintenance windows per quarter for Dedicated HA customers unless otherwise agreed.

5) Notice & traffic changes: we request 60 days' notice for sustained traffic pattern changes that increase peak QPS by >30% relative to onboarding profile. If such changes occur without notice, Redwood reserves the right to adjust capacity and associated pricing.

Next steps we propose: 
- Karen / Stellar legal to confirm the 25% cap and scoped carveouts in writing.
- If accepted, I'll push a final DocuSign via the link below (draft executed agreement with the Dedicated addendum as optional).

DocuSign draft: https://docusign.example.com/abcd-1234
Drive: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/SLA-drafts

If this is acceptable I'll prep a final version for signatures. Thanks — looking forward to closing this.

Best,
Diego
